notes: Condensed from the 0.5.0 cross-process session. Includes a decision reversal after a test failure.

messages.content: Multi-process writes still aren't safe. Fix it.
Decided: an OS-level advisory lock, fcntl on POSIX and msvcrt on Windows. Created graph_memory/filelock.py with one lock file per session.
does a lock alone fix it?
No. A worker holding a pre-prune view still writes its stale node set back, reinstating rows another worker deleted. The lock has to wrap a read-modify-write, not just the write.
so what does the reconcile do

Implemented _reconcile_with_disk in persistence.py. Under the lock it re-reads the stored row keys and adopts another process's deletions. Rows this instance created but never persisted are untouched.
Completed: four OS processes writing one session, 100 of 100 nodes persisted, zero lost. The stale writer no longer resurrects a prune.
Rate limiting, analytics and the semantic cache are still per-process, so limits apply per worker. Also flock is unreliable on NFS. Working on documenting both in the startup warning.
